description:
The helm deploy job now runs in `ghcr.io/sigterm-labs/images/k8s-deploy:latest`, or `:latest-vault` when `HELM_NEEDS_VAULT` is `"true"`.

- `.function.yml`: `image: $HELM_IMAGE` (defaults to `:latest`); a rule sets it to `:latest-vault` when `HELM_NEEDS_VAULT == "true"`.
- `.job.yml`: its own rules replace the inherited ones, so it repeats the vault rule scoped to the default branch.
- `HELM_VERSION` removed; it only selected the old `kubectl-helm` image tag.

Jobs extending `.helm_deploy` with their own `rules` need an equivalent rule to get the vault image (noted in the readme).

title: bot: Update SMS Import / Export to 10121
Draft: Answer an unknown access token with invalid_token across the API
description:
## What does this MR do and why?

On the REST API, a personal access token or OAuth token that GitLab cannot find gets the `401` of a request without a token: no `WWW-Authenticate` header and `{"message":"401 Unauthorized"}`. An expired or revoked token gets `invalid_token`, which [RFC 6750 section 3.1](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6750#section-3.1) defines for any token that is not valid.

Behind the `api_invalid_token_for_unknown_token` feature flag, the finders raise `TokenNotFoundError` instead of `UnauthorizedError` for such a token, and the API guard answers it as it answers an expired one: `invalid_token`, "Bad Access Token." and the challenge. `resolve_access_token` rescues the new error too, so a personal access token sent as a Bearer token, as the npm client does, is still found after the OAuth lookup misses. A personal access token disabled for the instance or an enterprise group is not found by that lookup either, so it gets the same answer. Web and GraphQL requests rescue every authentication error and are unchanged, as are the endpoints that use `authenticate_with`.

`API::Helpers::Mcp::AuthChallenge` no longer overrides `find_current_user!`, the override https://gitlab.com/orbit/gitlab/-/merge_requests/266878 added for the MCP endpoints. It turns the flag's behavior on for them whatever the flag's state, so an unknown token gets the same answer there as before. A token with no user, or whose composite identity cannot be resolved, now gets there the `401` every other endpoint gives it.

The flag has no rollout issue yet: I can open one from the template, or whoever rolls it out can.

<details><summary>Checks I ran</summary>

All on `master` at `08f81d7516a`, with Ruby 3.3 (3.3.11 and 3.3.12) rather than the 3.4.10 of `.ruby-version`:

- The changed spec files with `master`'s `auth_finders.rb` and `auth_challenge.rb`: 666 examples, 25 failures, 8 pending. The 25 are the examples that expect `TokenNotFoundError` or the `invalid_token` answer with the flag enabled. The examples with the flag disabled, and the MCP and Orbit ones in both states, pass there.
- The same files on the branch: 666 examples, 0 failures, 8 pending (skips inside the granular token shared examples).
- The specs that call or rescue the finders (request authenticator, API helpers and authentication, GraphQL, OAuth tokens, ActionCable connection, current organization, govern policies, usage data, the npm registries, the token resolver): 1920 examples, 4 failures, 20 pending. The 4 are GraphQL examples that render a page, and fail in my environment on `LoadError: cannot load such file -- sass`.
- RuboCop on the nine Ruby files: no offenses. Both commit message linters: no problems.

</details>

## References

Related to https://gitlab.com/orbit/gitlab/-/issues/637638

https://gitlab.com/orbit/gitlab/-/merge_requests/270914 changes the same line of `find_personal_access_token`; whichever merges second needs a one-line rebase.

## Screenshots or screen recordings

Not a UI change.

## How to set up and validate locally

1. Enable the feature flag in the Rails console:

   ```ruby
   Feature.enable(:api_invalid_token_for_unknown_token)
   ```

1. Send a request with a token GitLab does not know:

   ```shell
   curl --include --header "PRIVATE-TOKEN: <redacted> "http://gdk.test:3000/api/v4/user"
   ```

   The `401` carries `error="invalid_token"` in its `WWW-Authenticate` header and its body.
1. With the flag disabled, or without the header, the `401` is unchanged.

I did not follow these steps in a GDK; `spec/requests/api/api_guard_spec.rb` covers them with both states of the flag.

### [`v1.10.0`](https://github.com/github/github-mcp-server/releases/tag/v1.10.0): GitHub MCP Server 1.10.0

[Compare Source](https://github.com/github/github-mcp-server/compare/v1.9.0...v1.10.0)

#### Highlights

v1.10.0 is a substantial security, reliability, and compatibility release for the GitHub MCP Server.

##### Safer by default

- Added confirmed repository deletion with form elicitation and protected multi-round-trip state ([#​3076](https://github.com/github/github-mcp-server/pull/3076)).
- Restricted bearer credentials to configured GitHub authorities ([#​3056](https://github.com/github/github-mcp-server/pull/3056)).
- Enforced HTTPS for GitHub Enterprise hosts ([#​3069](https://github.com/github/github-mcp-server/pull/3069)).
- Made invalid static `--tools` configuration fail closed ([#​3050](https://github.com/github/github-mcp-server/pull/3050)).
- Hardened lockdown, request limits, cache isolation, URL traversal, and response sanitization ([#​3109](https://github.com/github/github-mcp-server/pull/3109), [#​3112](https://github.com/github/github-mcp-server/pull/3112), [#​3113](https://github.com/github/github-mcp-server/pull/3113), [#​3111](https://github.com/github/github-mcp-server/pull/3111), [#​3108](https://github.com/github/github-mcp-server/pull/3108), [#​3114](https://github.com/github/github-mcp-server/pull/3114), [#​3110](https://github.com/github/github-mcp-server/pull/3110)).

##### Better GitHub Enterprise Server compatibility

- `list_issues` and `search_issues` now degrade safely when issue custom-field GraphQL types are unavailable ([#​3086](https://github.com/github/github-mcp-server/pull/3086), [#​2897](https://github.com/github/github-mcp-server/pull/2897)).
- `list_issues` now returns assignee logins and stable empty arrays for unassigned issues ([#​3064](https://github.com/github/github-mcp-server/pull/3064)).
- Validation failures expose safe ruleset details when supplied by the GitHub API ([#​3081](https://github.com/github/github-mcp-server/pull/3081)).

##### Safer repository file operations

- `get_file_contents` now identifies symbolic links and clearly labels dereferenced content.
- Symbolic-link writes require explicit `allow_symlink_write: true` opt-in ([#​3071](https://github.com/github/github-mcp-server/pull/3071)).
- Fixed binary MCP resources being base64-encoded twice ([#​3098](https://github.com/github/github-mcp-server/pull/3098)).

##### More reliable tool contracts

- Corrected `add_issue_comment` input modes ([#​3085](https://github.com/github/github-mcp-server/pull/3085)).
- `issue_write.issue_fields[].delete: false` is now a valid no-op for strict-schema clients ([#​3077](https://github.com/github/github-mcp-server/pull/3077)).
- Zero-parameter tools accept an omitted `arguments` property while rejecting explicit `null` and malformed JSON ([#​3099](https://github.com/github/github-mcp-server/pull/3099)).
- Notification subscription tools explicitly advertise destructive behavior ([#​2936](https://github.com/github/github-mcp-server/pull/2936)).
- Copilot review-request denials now return actionable guidance instead of a bare 404 ([#​3119](https://github.com/github/github-mcp-server/pull/3119)).

##### Projects, Actions, and efficiency

- Added Project view lifecycle operations and visible-field configuration ([#​2961](https://github.com/github/github-mcp-server/pull/2961), [#​2988](https://github.com/github/github-mcp-server/pull/2988)).
- Reduced Actions and other successful response payloads ([#​3047](https://github.com/github/github-mcp-server/pull/3047), [#​3055](https://github.com/github/github-mcp-server/pull/3055)).
- Improved sanitization performance and refreshed UI/build dependencies ([#​3120](https://github.com/github/github-mcp-server/pull/3120), [#​3100](https://github.com/github/github-mcp-server/pull/3100)).

##### Behavior changes to note

- Unknown static `--tools` names now prevent startup.
- Symbolic-link updates require explicit opt-in.
- Requests cannot relax server-enforced lockdown.
- Oversized HTTP request bodies are rejected early.
- `add_issue_comment` performs stricter mutually exclusive mode validation.
- Repository deletion requires an eligible modern MCP client, form elicitation support, and the appropriate scopes.

### [`v1.1.0`](https://github.com/github/github-mcp-server/releases/tag/v1.1.0): GitHub MCP Server 1.1.0

[Compare Source](https://github.com/github/github-mcp-server/compare/v1.0.4...v1.1.0)

#### Highlights ✨

##### Insiders Mode: Issue Fields Support

Issue field support is now available behind the `remote_mcp_issue_fields` feature flag, and is enabled automatically in Insiders Mode. This includes listing issue fields, filtering issues by custom field values, and reading or writing issue field values.

##### Insiders Mode: CSV Output

CSV output for default `list_*` tools is now available behind the `csv_output` feature flag, and is enabled automatically in Insiders Mode. CSV provides a flatter, more compact representation for list-style responses, helping to reduce token usage for large result sets.

##### Context Reduction for GitHub Projects

Project item responses have been significantly reduced in size. `list_project_items`, `get_project_item`, and `update_project_item` now return compact project item, content, and field-value shapes instead of full GitHub issue and pull request payloads, cutting unnecessary context while preserving the information agents need.

##### Commit Search

A new `search_commits` tool has been added, allowing agents to search commits directly using GitHub search syntax. This fills a gap between listing repository commits and finding specific commits across debugging, auditing, and release investigation workflows.

##### GHAS Alert Pagination

The GHAS alert listing tools now support pagination. `list_code_scanning_alerts`, `list_dependabot_alerts`, and `list_secret_scanning_alerts` can now retrieve beyond the first page of results, avoiding incomplete alert summaries for repositories with larger security backlogs.

##### Reliability and Hardening

This release includes several tool reliability improvements, including returning `isError` for argument validation failures so agents can self-correct, guarding completions requests against malformed params, and ignoring proxy forwarding headers by default when building OAuth resource metadata.

A new opt-in mode for experimental tooling and features. The first experiment available through Insiders Mode is **MCP Apps** — see the [discussion](https://github.com/github/github-mcp-server/discussions/2048) for more details. Instructions for enabling Insiders Mode can be found in the [README](https://github.com/github/github-mcp-server?tab=readme-ov-file#insiders-mode).

Tool responses across multiple tools have been significantly trimmed, reducing context usage and improving efficiency for LLM interactions.
